observation_summary: The FastDateFormat.format(Date) method was incorrectly initializing the GregorianCalendar object using only the time zone, ignoring the locale. This caused incorrect week-of-year calculations when the system locale differed from the locale specified during FastDateFormat instantiation.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the initialization of the GregorianCalendar object to include the mLocale parameter. This is a classic case of incorrect initialization of an object's state, which directly impacts the subsequent computational logic (the week-of-year calculation). It is not a missing guard (Checking), nor a procedural rewrite (Algorithm/Method), nor a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the change: 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' was changed to 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'.
The bug report states: 'FastDateFormat apparently doesn't respect the locale it was sent on creation when outputting week in year... It seems to use the settings of the system locale'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The underlying algorithm for calculating the week is likely correct; the issue is that it was being fed a Calendar object initialized with the wrong locale settings.
This is a local fix to an existing method's initialization logic, not a design-level capability gap.
